freshness_caveat: Coal data stale as of 2025-12-26 (242 days old); Clean Dark stale as of 2025-12-31 (237 days old). Coal headline (7th-percentile) and Clean Dark spread (EUR 27.95/MWh, 47th-pctile) may not reflect current intra-day fuel-switch dynamics driven by Danube drought and heatwave.
risk_flags: EU storage at 63% full, 17.2pp below 5-yr seasonal mean — refill pace through autumn critical for winter adequacy and H2 2027 power costs.

GB power at 142.67 EUR/MWh (92nd-pctile) while DE power at 155.82 EUR/MWh (80th-pctile) — GB premium reflects isolation and intra-day constraint; vulnerable to renewable swings (daily change -41.33% on renewables).
Romanian Black Sea platform drone strike signals hybrid-warfare escalation on EU gas; knock-on TTF uplift if production disrupted; no quantified outage timeline yet.
Danube water crisis forces inland coal transport via costlier rail/truck; coal at 96 USD/t (7th-pctile, data stale Dec 26) masks regional supply tightness and hidden thermal cost inflation.

base.summary: Storage recovery modest; heatwave persists; Romanian platform stabilizes; US LNG growth dampens TTF baseline.

downside.summary: Romanian platform damage minimal; Danube recovers; US shale LNG accelerates; heatwave breaks and rainfall returns; storage refill pace accelerates.

upside.summary: Romanian offshore production outage confirmed; Danube barge transport halts; OPEC+ announces surprise supply cuts; heatwave extends.

themes: GB power spike amid tight EU storage and heating demand
Geopolitical supply threats: Romanian offshore gas, Iran sanctions
Danube drought forces coal-to-gas fuel switch; heatwave strains hydro
US shale LNG expansion bearish baseline; TTF at 74th-pctile on weather/sanctions upside
top_drivers: GB power at 92nd-pctile and DE power at 80th-pctile driven by tight EU storage (63% vs 80% seasonal norm), heatwave-constrained hydro, and Danube drought forcing coal-to-gas fuel switch.
Geopolitical supply risks: Romanian Black Sea platform drone strike and escalating Iran sanctions create upside tail on TTF via direct gas disruption and crude-LNG arb feedback.

US Permian shale LNG ramp and weak renewable share (43%, down 41.33% daily) provide baseline downside offset; coal at 7th-pctile reflects transportation and merit-order erosion from cheap gas displacement.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 92nd-percentile amid EU storage 17pp below seasonal; Romanian drone threat and Danube drought create gas/coal supply risks offsetting bearish US shale LNG expansion.

watchlist.why: Direct EU supply threat; drone attack signals hybrid warfare risk; production restart timeline and damage assessment will drive TTF risk premium and intra-EU flow allocation.

watchlist.metric: Danube water levels and coal barge logistics
watchlist.why: Low-water transport restrictions force fuel-switch to gas and pricier alternatives; Central European power margin compression; recovery timeline critical for Q4 thermal dispatch economics.

watchlist.metric: Iran sanctions regime and OPEC+ response
watchlist.why: Tighter Iran sanctions could support Brent, feeding crude-linked LNG arbs and potentially TTF uplift; OPEC+ meeting response (supply cuts vs. demand destruction) determines net oil-to-gas transmission.

watchlist.metric: European heatwave/drought relief and hydro recovery
watchlist.why: Sustained heat reduces hydro output and thermal cooling capacity; peaking plant dispatch tightens DA/ID spreads; wildfires risk transmission outages; relief timeline shapes power curve shape and regional scarcity rent.

watchlist.metric: US Permian shale production and LNG export ramp
watchlist.why: Higher US LNG supply capacity increases Atlantic arbitrage pressure on TTF; bearish baseline for EU gas and gas-fired power margins; export volumes and vessel availability lag supply growth, creating near-term upside volatility.

watchlist_dated.name: OPEC+ ministerial meeting (assumed imminence)
watchlist_dated.why: Iran sanctions and crude supply dynamics will shape OPEC+ cut response; outcome feeds LNG arb and TTF risk premium for weeks ahead.
